                  <ns0:p n="4">4 Then the King said unto me, For what dost thou make request? so I prayed to the God of heaven <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">To direct my thoughts and words, and to incline the Kings heart to grant my request.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And I said unto the king, If it please the king <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">My request whatsoever it is I humbly and wholly submit it to the Kings good pleasure being resolved to acquiesce in it.</ns0:note>, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">I pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tend no merit, but am an humble suppliant for thy grace and fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour, whereof having received some tokens I am thereby embol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dened to make this further request.</ns0:note>, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers sepulchers, that I may build it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And the king said unto me, (the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb</ns0:hi> wife.</ns0:note> queen also sitting by him <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Which is here noted, partly as an unusual thing; for common<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly the Kings of <ns0:hi>Persia</ns0:hi> dined alone, and their Queens seldom dined with them, as Historians note: and peradventure, because the Queen expressed some kindness to him and promoted his request with the King.</ns0:note>) For how long shall thy journey be! and when wilt thou return <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This question shewed the Kings respect and affection to him, and that he was not willing to want his attendance longer than was necessary.</ns0:note>? So it pleased the king to send me, and I set him a time <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Either that 12 years mentioned, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 5. 14. & 13. 6. or rather a far shorter time: for which cause<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> among others, he built the walls with such dispatch, even in 52 days, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 6. 15. and probably not very long after that returned to the King, by whom he was sent a second time with more ample Commission and for the Kings service and the Government of that part of his dominions.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7. Moreover, I said unto the king, If it please the king, let letters be given me to governours beyond the river, that they may convey me over <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">That they may safely conduct me through their several terri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tories.</ns0:note> till I come into Judah:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And a letter unto Asaph the keeper <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>of the kings orchard.</ns0:hi> So Gr.</ns0:note> of the kings forrest, <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Of the forest of <ns0:hi>Libanus</ns0:hi> famous for pleasure and for plenty of choice trees.</ns0:note> that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace, which <ns0:hi>appertained</ns0:hi> to the house <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">To wit of the Kings palace, which was adjoyning to the house of God. Or, <ns0:hi>of the Tower</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>sence</ns0:hi> belonging <ns0:hi>to the house of God,</ns0:hi> to wit, for the gates of the Courts of the Temple: for though the Temple was built, the Courts and other buildings be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />longing to the Temple might yet be unfinished.</ns0:note>, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Wherewith I may build an house in which I may dwell whilst I am there, and which I may dispose of as I see fit.</ns0:note>. And the king granted me, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezr. 7. 9.</ns0:note> ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the good hand of my God upon me.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 Then I came to the governours beyond the river, and gave them the kings letters. (Now the king had sent captains of the army, and horsemen with me.)</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 When Sanballat the Horonite <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">So called either from his family, or from the place of his birth or rule, which is supposed to be <ns0:hi>Horonaim,</ns0:hi> an eminent City of <ns0:hi>Moab, Isa.</ns0:hi> 15. 5. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 48. 3.</ns0:note>, and Tobiah the servant <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">So called probably from his ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vile original, or condition from which he was advanced to his pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent power and dignity: which also may be mentioned as one rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son why he now carried himself so insolently and perversly towards the Jews; it being, usual for Persons suddenly raised from a mean to an high estate so to demean themselves.</ns0:note> the Ammonite, heard <ns0:hi>of it,</ns0:hi> it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the wel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fare of the children of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Resting my self after my long journey and enquiring into the state of the City.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And I arose in the night <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Concealing both his intentions and actions as far and as long as he could, as knowing that the life of his business lay in secrecy, and expedition,</ns0:note>, I and some few men with me, neither told I <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> man what God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither <ns0:hi>was there any</ns0:hi> beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">To prevent noise and the notice of what I did.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And I went out by night <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The footmen which accompanied him directing and leading him in the way. His design was to go round about the City, to ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serve the compass and condition of the Walls and Gates, that he might make sufficient provisions for the work.</ns0:note>, by the gate of the valley <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Of which see <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 3. 13.</ns0:note>, even before the dragon-well <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">A fountain or water so called either from some figure of a Dragon or Serpent which was by it: or from some living Dra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gon which abode there when the City was desolate: for Dragons delight to be in desolate places<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and nigh to springs of water, as divers have observed.</ns0:note>, and to the dung<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />port <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Through which they used to carry the dung out of the City.</ns0:note>, and viewed the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and the gates thereof were consumed with fire.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:369" />14 Then I went on to the gate of the fountain <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Which led to the fountain, to wit, of <ns0:hi>Siloah</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Gihon.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and to the kings pool <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">That which King <ns0:hi>Hezekiah</ns0:hi> had made: of which see 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 32. 3. 30.</ns0:note>: but <ns0:hi>there was</ns0:hi> no place for the beast <ns0:hi>that was</ns0:hi> under me to pass <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The way being obstructed with heaps of rubbish.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 Then went I up in the night by the brook <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Of <ns0:hi>Kidron;</ns0:hi> of which see on 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 15. 23.</ns0:note>, and viewed the wall, and turned back, and entred by the gate of the valley, and <ns0:hi>so</ns0:hi> returned <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Having gone found about the City.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 And the rulers knew not whither I went, or what I did, neither had I as yet told it to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest that did <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>were to do,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>should do, i. e.</ns0:hi> Whom he intended to im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ploy in it.</ns0:note> the work <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Here following of building the Walls.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> in, how Jerusalem <ns0:hi>lieth</ns0:hi> waste, and the gates thereof are burnt with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />proach.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the kings words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for <ns0:hi>this</ns0:hi> good <ns0:hi>work.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian <ns0:hi>i</ns0:hi> heard <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> this thing that ye do? Will ye rebel a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst the king <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Do you design to fortify this City against the King?</ns0:note>? <ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>k</ns0:hi> Either the Kings Lieutenant in <ns0:hi>Arabia,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Tobiah</ns0:hi> was among the <ns0:hi>Ammonites,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi> among the <ns0:hi>Moabites:</ns0:hi> Or rather an <ns0:hi>Arabian</ns0:hi> by his birth. And it seems probable that both he, and <ns0:hi>Sanballat,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Tobiah</ns0:hi> were chief men or Governours among the <ns0:hi>Samaritans,</ns0:hi> or in their Army. See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 4. 1, 2, 3.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 Then answered I them, and said unto them, The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ezra 4. 3.</ns0:note> ye have no por<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, nor right <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">You have no authority over us, nor interest in our Church or State, or City, but are meer aliens from the Common-Wealth of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> We disown and detest that mungrel-Worship and Religion which you have set up. We desire not your favour, or friendship, or help in this matter. And you have nothing to do to enquire into, or meddle with our concerns, or to hinder us in our present undertaking.</ns0:note>, nor memorial <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Here no Testimony or Monument either of your Relation to us by Birth or Religion, or of your kindness to us or to this place. But we have many memorials of your Malice and En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mity against us.</ns0:note> in Jerusalem.</ns0:p>
